title: 3 ways to plan for electricity increases #Budget
text:
First: give electricity its own line in your budget, with a raise every year; when your municipality's increase comes in July, or Eskom's in April, add about 9% to that line. Second: watch your units, not just your rand: write down how many units R500 buys this month and check again next July. Third: if your household income is low, ask your municipality whether you qualify for free basic electricity (often 50 units a month; the new pricing policy approved by Cabinet in August 2026 proposes 200 to 300 units for qualifying households, but that is still a proposal).

Full guide: "How Eskom Went Broke, and What It Costs You Every Month (South Africa 2026)" on the Money From Zero channel.

Sources
- NERSA decisions, via EWN (10 Feb 2026) and Enerdata (16 Mar 2026)
- Revised electricity pricing policy, approved by Cabinet, August 2026
